chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about a man who has a qamīs: should he be shrouded in it? He said, "Cut off its buttons."

I said: "And its sleeves?" He said, "No. That only applies when it is cut for him and it is new; sleeves should not be made for it. But if it is a worn garment, nothing is cut from it except the buttons."

key_terms.أَيُكَفَّنُ: whether he is to be shrouded in it
key_terms.الْقَمِيصُ: the shirt or tunic used here in the context of shrouding the deceased
key_terms.ثَوْبًا لَبِيسًا: a garment that has already been worn

ai.seo_question: Should a deceased person be shrouded in a shirt, and should its buttons and sleeves be removed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on using a shirt as part of a deceased person's shroud. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that the buttons should be removed, while the sleeves are only omitted if the garment is newly prepared for burial; if it is a previously worn garment, only the buttons are removed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.415 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about whether a man should be shrouded in his shirt (Qamis).
Imam (as) said: "Remove its buttons."

I asked: "And the sleeves?"
Imam (as) said: "No, that is only necessary if it is made new for him, in which case it should have no sleeves. However, if it is an already-worn garment, only the buttons need to be removed."
